text:
The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office finally put a price tag on the Iran war. Roughly $38 billion in the first five months alone, and another $2 to $3 billion for every month it drags on.

Even that figure doesn’t tell the whole story. 

It excludes repairs to U.S. bases damaged in the fighting and the interest on the money we're borrowing to pay for all of it. The Pentagon's own latest number to Congress is at least $42 billion.

Then Americans pay a second time, at the pump and at the checkout line. 

CBO projects the war will push inflation up half a point by early 2027, driven by energy costs. 

Diesel just hit a record national average.

Congress never authorized this war. The House has voted again and again to end it. Enough is enough.
https://t.co/45GeIXzWCP

text:
One of the most powerful experiences I’ve had in 21 months as your Member of Congress was visiting the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency at Pearl Harbor and seeing firsthand the commitment our nation has made to identify, bring home, and reunite missing servicemembers with their families. On National POW/MIA Recognition Day, we honor the brave men and women who were held captive or who are still missing in their service to our country – including many of whom were never given a proper chance to be laid to rest. 

To this day, over 900 Marylanders who served in World War I, World War II, Korea, and Vietnam have been declared missing in action. Today and everyday, we remember the lives lost and stand with the families who never received closure for their loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. It’s why I’m committed to fighting to restore vital funding of the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency to continue its most sacred mission. If my office can be of assistance, please reach out to (410) 832-8890.

If @POTUS wants to use our public lands for data centers, he’s going to have to answer to the American people who are overwhelmingly against such a move. 

The first step is to disclose where in Nevada, Arizona, Utah, Oregon and Idaho the administration is planning data centers on public land, as reported in the Washington Sun. The public has a right to know. 

We’ve already seen in Boulder City that the Trump Administration is willing to sidestep the law in order to build his data center pet projects without public input or a proper environmental review. 

That is why I introduced my Public Lands Accountability Act to ensure the public’s voice is heard and that the effects on the environment, water resources and the electric grid are thoroughly assessed and made public.

text:
Getting the spent nuclear fuel off our coastline has been a top priority of mine for as long as I've served in Congress, and it will stay that way for as long as it takes. There is no question that this fuel needs to move as quickly and safely as possible.

When I got to Congress in 2019, there was no plan to move it. 

The federal government was supposed to start taking this waste in 1998 and never did. 

Yucca Mountain, the only site Congress ever picked, was shut down in 2009, and nothing replaced it. Months before I took office, a canister nearly fell 18 feet during loading. In sum, I inherited a bad situation.

One of my first steps was bringing experts and community leaders together on a SONGS Task Force. They presented findings and recommendations that have guided my work ever since.

I brought Democrats and Republicans together in the Spent Nuclear Fuel Solutions Caucus to restart a stalled national conversation. I’ve met regularly with Department of Energy staff, including earlier this week, to discuss the new path forward.

Through the House Appropriations process, I've helped secure over $250 million for this work. 

That includes Atlas, a new railcar built to carry spent fuel safely across the country by rail. The funding we secured supported the last administration's work to find willing host communities through a collaborative siting program. It also is assisting the new Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, a continuation of this work, with six states already signing up.

I’ve also introduced several pieces of bipartisan legislation that provide a strong roadmap for the future, including language to prioritize the movement of spent fuel from sites like ours, and to create a new sole purpose entity for the management of spent fuel nationwide.

There is much work ahead, but I’m greatly encouraged by our progress. 

I'll be sharing a more comprehensive update in coming weeks.
https://t.co/zb73WpzUmX

When hospitals close their labor and delivery units, pregnant patients are forced to travel farther and farther from home to access the care they need. For rural communities, the distance can mean the difference between life and death.

As maternity care deserts grow and the maternal mortality crisis worsens due to federal funding cuts and our country continues to face a maternal mortality crisis, we must ensure that every hospital can provide maternity care. During a Health Care Subcommittee hearing, I discussed how the Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act that I cosponsor will help.

Janine and I are horrified by the brutal attack on Mr. Singh, a Sikh truck driver and member of our Sacramento community who was stabbed 17 times at a rest stop in Wyoming. 

We are praying for his full recovery and grateful to the family whose quick actions helped save his life.

Law enforcement has not identified a motive, but we cannot ignore the troubling rise in hate and rhetoric targeting Sikh and South Asian Americans across our nation. 

Just days before this attack, the Department of Homeland Security posted a racist caricature of a Sikh truck driver telling "Mr. Singh" to "get off our roads" and "self-deport or find out."

Rhetoric from the highest levels of our government carries weight. 

When administration officials use the power and platform of the federal government to single out Sikh identity and portray an entire community as dangerous, unwanted, or less American, they fan the flames of hate and reinforce stereotypes that can have real-life consequences for Sikh Americans and the broader South Asian community.

Violence and hate against Sikh Americans, South Asian Americans, or any community must be unequivocally condemned. 

Sacramento stands with Mr. Singh and the Sikh community.
https://t.co/NSsMD4o1rv

In July, I sent a letter to @JosephMLombardo calling on him to pause state tax abatements for data centers on public lands until the 2027 Nevada Legislature had an opportunity to review the issue.  

I am glad that the Governor is recognizing the need for these projects to pay into our education system and contribute to our community. The larger issue, though, is whether we want to provide tax breaks to an industry that could strain our limited water resources and create large new demands on our electrical grid.

text:
Yesterday, I joined @RepMGS and my PA House Democratic colleagues in demanding transparency from the largest ICE detention center in the Northeast.

As ICE tries to extend the use of this facility for another ten years, Pennsylvanians deserve answers about where our taxpayer dollars are going.

quoted.text:
Today I led PA House Dems in pressing ICE, GEO, and Clearfield County, Pennsylvania, for transparency on the use of taxpayer dollars to fund the private prison company that runs Moshannon Valley Processing Center, the largest detention center in the Northeast.

The private prison company has reported record profits driven by this Administration’s mass deportation and immigrant surveillance campaigns. Over $5 million per month is spent at Moshannon to imprison more than 1,600 people, the majority of whom have NO CRIMINAL CHARGES. Federal law is clear that immigration detention is only for the purpose of ensuring attendance at hearings and for imminent deportation.  Some of those sent to Moshannon were detained when they showed up for their hearings!

The private prison company uses people our government has detained to do most of the labor at the “processing center.” Meanwhile, reports of inadequate food and medical care, sexual harassment, and at least three detainee deaths indicate that the processing center may be violating basic humanitarian standards.

As Members of Congress, we are responsible for conducting oversight to ensure that taxpayer dollars are spent wisely and well.  We also represent constituents (a term that includes all who reside in our districts) who have been detained at Moshannon, and we have a responsibility to ensure their rights are not violated. https://t.co/lUzO8uM10G

This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation, it is about making sure — with warning signs flashing red — that we can safely deploy AI, and win the race the right way.

Today at @FDUWhatsNew, I announced a bipartisan plan to put real guardrails on AI — and keep America ahead in the AI race. 

The American AI Security Act, which I’m introducing with @RepMikeLawler, would require mandatory, time-bound, pre-deployment national security reviews before the most powerful AI models go out the door.

The China FIREWALL Act, which I’m introducing with @RepLaLota, would close a loophole allowing the government to use Chinese AI models. I already got DeepSeek banned from most federal devices, and this would close the loophole for good. If we don't trust Beijing with our data, we shouldn't trust their AI.

We can't bury our heads in the sand, and we can't hand the future to China. We have to put real guardrails in place, and compete like hell to win.

text:
Nike and Converse, what the hell were you thinking?

Your campaign shows what looks like a hooded Klansman, framed by what appears to be the dangling feet of a lynching victim. There is nothing creative or artistic about it. It is racist, reckless and deeply offensive.

I am a Black man, a son of the South and a Member of Congress from Louisiana. Where I come from, the image of Black people hanging from trees is not ancient history. That pain still lives in our families and communities. The white hood is not some harmless costume. It is a symbol of terror, murder and generations of racial violence.

Do not insult our intelligence by dismissing this as an unfortunate misunderstanding. An advertising campaign does not just appear. It is conceived, photographed, reviewed, approved and distributed. At every stage, someone had the opportunity—and the responsibility—to say no.

Who created this campaign? Who approved it? How many executives saw it? Were there any Black people in the room? If so, did anyone listen to them?

You do not get to quietly pull the images, issue a polished apology and move on. You do not get a do-over. The public deserves to know how this happened, who was responsible and what you intend to do about it.

Black pain is not a marketing prop. Lynching is not a creative concept. The Ku Klux Klan is not an aesthetic.

This campaign should never have been created, approved or released. Nike and Converse must answer for it. You have caused real harm, and repairing that harm will require more than an apology written by your public relations department.

@Nike @converse @blackcaucus @USProgressives @HouseDemocrats @MSNOWNews @NAACP_LDF @NAACP @TheRevAl

Gracias por este gran reconocimiento.

text:
Friday in the First

Michael Johnson, II, a student at Elizabeth City State University, is already finding meaningful ways to serve the community he now calls home. Through his work at the Elizabeth City Senior Center, Michael helps create a welcoming environment where older adults can stay active, connect with their neighbors, and access local programs and resources.

Michael reminds us that you do not have to wait until graduation to make a difference. By giving his time and energy to others while pursuing his education at ECSU, he is building connections across generations and strengthening the community around him.

We are proud to recognize Michael Johnson II for his commitment to serving Elizabeth City and helping make his community a more welcoming and connected place for residents of all ages.

#FridaySpotlight

text: Proud that my bipartisan, bicameral SEED Act has been signed into law to support our pre-K educators! Early childhood educators routinely dip into their own pockets for classroom supplies but until now were denied the same educator expense deduction available to K–12 teachers. This new law closes that gap, delivers long-overdue tax relief, and recognizes the essential role these educators play in giving our youngest learners a strong start.
